name: Aquasky RGB II
summary: ADA's slim RGB LED that stands on legs outside the glass of a 60 cm tank. It is controlled over Bluetooth from ADA's phone app, with colour, brightness and timer settings, and a soft fade on and off.
bestFor: A 60 cm planted tank where you want strong, tunable light and a clean ADA look without a separate controller.
highlights: 70 RGB LEDs, up to 40,000 lux at 10 cm
Draws up to 66 W at full output
Legs rest outside the glass, so any glass thickness works on a 60 cm wide tank
Bluetooth app control with presets, colour tuning and a timer
Flicker-free, which helps when filming or photographing the tank

specs.Colour temperature: About 8,000 to 11,000 K in default mode

watchOut: It is made for 60 cm tanks only, and full power is a lot of light for a low-tech tank without CO2.

name: CB Ultrathin LED
summary: A basic, very thin white LED bar with extendable brackets that rest on the tank rim. Five lengths from 50 to 140 cm.
bestFor: Low-tech planted and community tanks where you just need decent white light.
watchOut: No dimming, timer or published PAR, and wattage per length drops off on the longest bars.

name: CL Clamp Lamp
summary: Small clamp-on lamps with an adjustable aluminium head. The P models take PL compact fluorescent tubes, the L models use LEDs. Old-school but fine for a nano.
bestFor: Nano and small tanks with low-light plants.
highlights: PL fluorescent (5 to 13 W) or LED (1.2 to 2.2 W)
watchOut: The LED versions are very low wattage and will only grow the easiest plants.

name: CM-10 LED Clip Light
summary: A compact clip-on LED panel with touch control and several lighting modes. Runs on a low-voltage adaptor.
bestFor: Nano tanks and desktop scapes with easy plants.
watchOut: No spectrum or PAR data published.

name: ZN WiFi LED
summary: A slim aluminium LED bar with app control over timing, brightness and colour, including a 24-hour sunrise-to-sunset cycle. There is also an IR remote.
bestFor: Planted tanks from 45 to 90 cm where you want scheduling and colour control on a budget.
highlights: App control of timer, brightness and colour
watchOut: Boyu gives no PAR or lumen data, and lists the ZN-60 at the same length as the ZN-45, which looks like a sheet error.

name: ZN-800 / ZN-1600 Arm LED
summary: Fan-cooled LED spots on a gooseneck arm that clamps to the tank edge. The ZN-800 is a single puck, the ZN-1600 a twin-lens bar with app control. Knobs let you dim and shift the colour temperature.
bestFor: Open-top tanks where you want a hanging-style look without a ceiling mount.
watchOut: The colour dial runs between blue and white, which hints at a marine focus, and there is no PAR data.

name: A II Max
summary: A brighter, bigger sibling of the A II with nearly double the output per size and a wider size range up to 140 cm tanks. It ships on metal legs, and Chihiros sells acrylic legs and a hanging kit if you want a different look.
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks from nano to large that want a simple, bright, app-controlled bar at a fair price.
highlights: Six sizes covering 30 cm to 140 cm tanks
Up to 8,100 lm on the 1201 Max
Bluetooth app: brightness, timer and schedules
Metal legs as standard; hanging kit and acrylic legs available

specs.Mounting: Metal rim legs (acrylic legs and hanging kit optional)

watchOut: The retailer pitches its spectrum at low-tech scapes, so it is less suited to showing off red plants than an RGB light.

name: A II Series
summary: A very slim Chihiros bar on clear acrylic clamp legs that can swivel, so you can angle the light toward one part of the scape. Output is moderate and the spectrum leans toward red and blue, with Bluetooth app control built in.
bestFor: Nano and small low to medium light tanks where you want app control and a nearly invisible fixture.
highlights: Four sizes for 30, 36, 45 and 60 cm tanks
8000 K full spectrum weighted to red and blue

specs.Spectrum: Full spectrum, weighted to red and blue

watchOut: Clamps fit glass up to 8 mm only, and output is modest for carpets without CO2.

name: B Series
summary: Chihiros' straightforward WRGB bar: white LEDs with a few RGB diodes mixed in, adjustable legs and Bluetooth control. It is a no-fuss light for everyday planted tanks, available in seven lengths.
bestFor: Low to medium demand planted tanks and beginners who want app scheduling without spending much.
highlights: Seven sizes from 20 cm to 120 cm
White plus RGB LEDs for natural colour
Bluetooth app for brightness and timers
Adjustable legs; shade and hanging kit sold separately
watchOut: Models up to B60 only clamp glass up to 8 mm (12 mm for larger ones), and B80 specs weren't listed by the retailer.

name: C II Series
summary: A compact clamp-on light on a vertical pole, so you can set both height and angle over a nano tank. It comes in a white version or an RGB version.
bestFor: Small nano tanks and open-top bowls where one compact, adjustable light is enough.
highlights: White (1,500 lm) or RGB (1,580 lm) versions
Adjustable height and swivel on a pole clamp
Bluetooth app for brightness, schedule, sunrise/sunset and colour (RGB model)
Optional base for use away from a tank
watchOut: The clamp fits glass up to 8 mm only, and the display base is an extra purchase.

name: C Series
summary: A simple clip-on nano light that hangs over the tank on a short arm. It is inexpensive, easy to fit and bright enough for small planted tanks.
bestFor: Nano tanks from roughly 8 to 38 L with easy to moderate plants.
highlights: Four sizes for 20 to 36 cm tanks
Clip-on arm for rimless glass up to 6 mm
watchOut: Only fits glass up to 6 mm thick, and it has no app control.

name: Magnetic Light 2
summary: A palm-sized round puck light with a magnetic back, meant to stick to a metal stand or the included adhesive plate. It has a small cooling fan and mixes RGB and white LEDs, with control through the Chihiros app.
bestFor: Tiny tanks, or spotlighting a single plant or stone where a bar light won't fit.
highlights: App control of brightness, colour channels and sunrise/sunset
Magnetic mounting with adhesive metal pad included
watchOut: You need a metal stand or surface to mount it, and at around 800 lm it only lights a small footprint.

name: Nano Universal RGB
summary: A clip-on RGB nano light in two sizes, made for 20 to 36 cm tanks. It is fully waterproof to IP67 and has Bluetooth control, so it handles a humid open-top nano without complaint.
bestFor: Shrimp tanks, betta tanks and small planted nanos that want colour control in a compact clip-on.
highlights: Nano 20 and Nano 30 sizes for 20 to 36 cm tanks
Bluetooth app: brightness, timer, spectrum and effects
Clips on glass up to 10 mm
watchOut: Two sizes only, so anything past 36 cm needs a different light.

name: RGB Vivid II (10th Edition)
summary: The compact but very powerful RGB panel that made the Vivid name, here in its 10th Edition. It packs 130 W and over 12,000 lm into a 45.5 cm panel meant for 60 to 90 cm tanks, the same body size as the Vivid II Mate. It is being phased out in favour of the Vivid Mini and Vivid 3.
bestFor: Tall or demanding high-tech tanks where one small panel has to deliver a lot of light.
highlights: App control of colour, brightness and sunrise/sunset
watchOut: Discontinued, and the stand or hanging kit shown in photos is sold separately.

name: RGB Vivid II Mate
summary: A pared-back version of the Vivid II with fewer LEDs, keeping the same shape, app and full RGB channel control. At 125 W it still has far more output than most 60 to 90 cm tanks need, and it comes with a hanging kit.
bestFor: High-tech 60 to 90 cm tanks, especially deeper ones, where you want a pendant with lots of headroom.
highlights: One fixture for 60 to 90 cm tanks
Individual RGB channel control in the MyChihiros app
watchOut: Expensive, and you will rarely run it near full power without inviting algae.

name: RGB Vivid Mini
summary: A compact 35 cm RGB panel with 75 W of output, sold either with a rim-mounted bar or as a pendant with a hanging kit. It brings Vivid-level colour and punch to smaller high-tech tanks.
bestFor: Smaller high-tech tanks, or deeper nanos, where you want strong RGB colour from a compact panel.
highlights: RGB LEDs with full app control of colour and effects
Standard rim bar or pendant version
Optional WiFi hub for remote control
watchOut: The shade is sold separately, and the pendant version comes without the rim-mount bar.

name: WRGB II Pro
summary: The high-output member of the WRGB II family, with a dedicated white channel on top of full RGB and a higher LED count. It is still slim, and gives strong light and colour for demanding scapes.
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks and deeper aquariums where you want lots of output and control over colour.
highlights: Six sizes from 30 cm to 120 cm
Up to 11,170 lm on the Pro 120
White plus RGB channels, each adjustable in the app
watchOut: More light than a low-tech tank can use; dim it right down if you don't run CO2.

name: WRGB II Slim
summary: A thinner, lower-output take on the WRGB II with full colour control in the app. At about 1.5 cm thick, it disappears over a rimless tank and suits most planted setups from low to fairly demanding.
bestFor: Everyday planted tanks where you want RGB colour tuning and a very low-profile fixture.
highlights: Five sizes from 30 cm to 120 cm
WRGB with app control of colour and brightness
watchOut: Only about a third to two-fifths of the output of the matching WRGB II Pro, so it is less suited to deep high-tech tanks.

name: WRGB Vivid 3
summary: Chihiros' flagship planted-tank light, a wide flat panel only 23 mm thick with a snap-on magnetic fan. Output now goes up to 180 W and 16,600 lm, which is serious light for tall or large high-tech scapes.
bestFor: Large or deep high-tech tanks with CO2 where you want maximum light and colour tuning from one fixture.
highlights: WRGB with white plus RGB 3-in-1 LEDs
App control of brightness, colour, timing and fan
watchOut: Very expensive and very powerful; smaller or low-tech tanks will struggle to use it well.

name: Z Light Tiny
summary: A tiny clip-on spotlight with a zoom lens, used to pick out a single plant, stone or focal point. The Diving Edition can even go underwater for shadow and uplighting effects.
bestFor: Adding highlights or accent lighting to a nano or display tank alongside a main light.
highlights: Diving Edition is IP67 and submersible

specs.Mounting: Clip-on (extension arm and extra clip sold as accessories)

watchOut: It is an accent light, not a main light for growing plants; only the Diving Edition may be submerged.

name: LED 109 Clip Light
summary: A slim 3.4 W clip-on LED with 12 white and 3 blue diodes on an arched arm. It clamps to glass up to 5 mm thick.
bestFor: A small nano with low-light plants such as Anubias, Bucephalandra, Java fern and mosses.
watchOut: Too weak for carpeting plants or red stems; treat it as a viewing light that keeps easy plants ticking over.

name: Mini LED Clip Light
summary: Small clip-on lights for tiny tanks: a gooseneck 8-LED spot and flat 10, 14 and 20 LED panels on a swivel clamp.
bestFor: Lighting a desktop tank or betta setup with a few low-light plants.

specs.Mount: Clip-on (gooseneck on 8 LED, swivel clamp on the others)

watchOut: Wattage and spectrum are not published; expect only enough light for the hardiest plants.

name: powerRGB
summary: powerRGB is a low-voltage RGB LED bar meant to sit alongside your main light and add colour. Paired with the RGBcontrol+e controller (sold separately) you can blend colours, run sunrise and sunset, and add moonlight.
bestFor: Tanks that already have a white main light and where you want richer reds and greens, or smooth dawn and dusk.
highlights: Adds red, green and blue to lift plant and fish colour
Three lengths for tanks from about 79 to 125 cm
watchOut: It is a supplementary light, not a full planted-tank light on its own, and the colour control needs an extra controller.

name: HeliaLux Spectrum
summary: Juwel's step-up LED bar, with white LEDs at 9,000 K and 6,500 K plus red, green and blue channels. It drops into any Juwel tank with a fixed top frame, and a UniversalFit holder lets it sit on other tanks too. Compared with the stock MultiLux it adds colour channels and, with the SmartControl or AppControl added, dimming and scheduling.
bestFor: Juwel tank owners who want to grow a wider range of plants than the stock MultiLux allows.
highlights: Eight lengths from 55 to 150 cm to match Juwel tanks
White plus RGB LEDs for plant growth and better colour rendering
About 140 lumens per watt, with aluminium honeycomb heat sinks
Scratch-resistant safety glass over the LEDs

specs.LEDs: White 9,000 K and 6,500 K plus red, green and blue
specs.Mounting: Juwel tanks with fixed top frame; UniversalFit holder for other tanks

watchOut: Dimming, sunrise and colour control need the HeliaLux SmartControl or AppControl, sold separately.

name: MultiLux LED
summary: The standard light unit fitted to Juwel's LED aquariums, holding two replaceable glass LED tubes (one DAY, one NATURE). It is sealed against moisture and lets you work in the tank with the light on. Buying one on its own makes sense for replacing a T5 unit or a broken lid light.
bestFor: Juwel owners converting from T5 or replacing a lid light for a low-light planted or community tank.
highlights: Eight lengths from 55 to 150 cm to fit Juwel tanks
Two replaceable LED tubes, 9,000 K and 6,500 K
Moisture-blocking membrane keeps the unit dry
Roughly half the energy of the old T5 units

specs.Tubes: 2 x replaceable Juwel LED tubes (DAY and NATURE fitted)

watchOut: There is no dimming or scheduling built in, so plan on a plug-in timer, or look at the HeliaLux Spectrum if you want control.

name: HighLine Classic LED
summary: A slim, fully waterproof LED tube in a 6,500 K daylight tone, made as the lighting for Oase HighLine aquariums. Each tube has its own on/off switch and is IP68 rated, and it fits other tanks with compatible holders. HighLine tanks are usually lit with two of these side by side.
bestFor: HighLine owners, or anyone wanting simple, waterproof daylight tubes for a low to medium-light tank.
highlights: IP68 waterproof with inline toggle switch
Daylight spectrum suited to plants and natural colours
watchOut: No dimming or scheduling on its own; you will want a plug-in timer.

name: MotionControl LED
summary: Oase's controllable LED bar with four channels: neutral white, cool white, royal blue and red. Through the Oase aquarium controller and app you can set colour and intensity by segment and run sunrise and sunset effects. It is freshwater only and IP68 sealed, with a thin 15 mm profile.
bestFor: Keepers with an Oase HighLine or ScaperLine who want app-controlled, adjustable-spectrum lighting.
highlights: Neutral white, cool white, royal blue and red LEDs
Segment-by-segment colour and brightness control via app
IP68 waterproof, no condensation inside the housing

specs.Channels: Neutral white, cool white, royal blue, red
specs.Control: Oase aquarium controller and app (sold separately); IR control set optional
specs.Power supply: Oase Control Aquarium Transformer 120 W (sold separately)

watchOut: Colour and segment control needs the Oase aquarium controller, and power comes from the separate 120 W Control transformer, so the real cost is higher than the bar alone.

name: ADE LED Light
summary: A slim 63 mm wide LED bar for tanks from about 28 to 113 cm, with more output per length than the ADP. Six sizes from 12 to 28 W.
bestFor: Low to medium light planted tanks on a budget.
highlights: Six sizes for tanks 28 to 113 cm

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

watchOut: Brightness does not scale much with length (28 W at 90 cm), so longer tanks get less light per litre.

name: ADF LED Light
summary: A wide 22.5 cm LED panel-bar for big tanks from 70 to 150 cm, from 45 to 90 W. The width spreads light across deeper tanks better than a narrow strip.
bestFor: Larger planted tanks that need a bright, wide light.
highlights: Four sizes for tanks 70 to 150 cm

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

name: ADP Slim LED Light
summary: A very slim (7 mm) LED bar on adjustable legs, in 11 lengths from 8 cm up to 110 cm. It is the light SunSun pairs with its HEK and HWK open tanks.
bestFor: Low-tech planted tanks, shrimp tanks and fish-only setups that want a neat, low-profile light.

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

watchOut: Output is low for the size (about 16 W on a 100 cm tank), so it is for easy, low-light plants only.

name: ADS LED Light
summary: A 10 cm wide LED bar for tanks from 38 to 130 cm, in fixed C7 aquatic versions and dimmable T versions. The larger C7 models reach 60 to 80 W.
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks where you want a single bar with decent output.
highlights: C7 aquatic versions from 14 to 80 W

specs.Mount: Adjustable legs on the tank rim

watchOut: The H (sea light) versions in the same range are for marine tanks; pick C7 or T for plants.

name: ADT Round Clip Light
summary: A round 20 cm LED disc on a clamp arm, made in freshwater versions of 48 and 80 W. The 100C is the brighter 'glare' version for 60 to 80 cm tanks.
bestFor: Mid-size open-top planted tanks where a single bright light is enough.
highlights: Clamps to glass up to 20 mm
watchOut: SunSun also sells H (seawater) versions of this light; make sure you pick the C models for a planted tank.

name: ADT-2 Stand Light
summary: A cube-shaped LED spotlight on a rim-mounted arm, with vents on three sides for cooling. The 240C and 260C let you adjust brightness and colour temperature, covering tanks from 30 to 60 cm.
bestFor: Small open-top planted tanks where you want a strong, focused light.
highlights: Two colour modes, adjustable on 240C and 260C
Clamps to glass 5 to 18 mm thick
watchOut: A single spotlight suits roughly cube-shaped tanks better than long, shallow ones.

name: ADT-3 Stand Light
summary: A larger aluminium spotlight for 40 to 80 cm tanks, with adjustable power and colour temperature and two switchable modes. It hangs from a T3 rim-mounted stand.
bestFor: Medium open-top planted tanks that need more punch than a nano light.
watchOut: Spotlights can leave the corners of a rectangular tank darker than the centre.

name: ADT-880C Panel Light
summary: A flat 58 × 30 cm LED panel held over the tank on two stand brackets, rated for tanks up to 120 cm. Power and colour temperature are adjustable up to 80 W.
bestFor: Open-top planted tanks where you want a wide, even spread from one fixture.
watchOut: At 58 cm long, a 120 cm tank will have darker ends; it works best on tanks near its own length.

name: ADT-I Nano Stand Light
summary: A small cylindrical LED spotlight hung from an arm that clamps to the tank rim, sized for nano and small tanks from 20 to 60 cm. SunSun ships it with several of its tanks, and it gives an open-top tank a clean, gallery look.
bestFor: Nano planted tanks and small shrimp setups with an open top.
highlights: Clamps to glass 5 to 18 mm thick

specs.Mount: Clamp-on stand arm (T1 or T2 bracket)

watchOut: One puck light gives a pool of light rather than even coverage, so the edges of a wider tank stay dimmer.

name: ADZ Metal LED Spotlight
summary: A small metal-bodied mains LED spotlight (4.5 cm across) in 3, 5 and 7 W, with warm or three-colour adjustable white. It works as an accent light over an open nano tank.
bestFor: Accent lighting on a small open-top nano, or picking out a focal stone or plant alongside a main light.
watchOut: SunSun gives no mounting details or tank sizing, so plan how you will hang or aim it.

name: AMD Hang-On Nano Light
summary: A tiny USB-powered (5 V) LED that hooks over thin glass, for nano tanks up to about 50 cm. The AD-150 is a small clip-on lamp for tanks under 30 cm.
bestFor: Betta tanks, pico scapes and shrimp cubes with easy plants.
watchOut: Only fits thin glass (5 mm or less) and is a low-light option.

name: Dream White Plant Tube Light
summary: A sealed tube light from SunSun's Dream range, in the white version made for aquatic plants. It comes in six lengths for tanks from 80 cm to 2 m.
bestFor: Large tanks that already have a lid and want a simple plant-oriented tube.
watchOut: Output is low for the tank sizes it targets (30 W for 2 m), so treat it as a supplement or for undemanding plants.

name: ZDO Amphibious Tube Light
summary: A sealed LED tube that can run in or out of water, from SunSun's Zhizhen line, for tanks from 1.2 m upward. Four lengths from 98 to 170 cm.
bestFor: Big lidded fish tanks that want extra or replacement lighting.
watchOut: Low output for such long tanks; it will not drive a demanding planted setup on its own.

name: A Series
summary: Twinstar's entry-level light, a thin WRGB bar on an adjustable bracket so one unit can span a range of tank lengths. Output is modest, which makes it a fair match for fish-first tanks and easy plants rather than carpets.
bestFor: Beginners and low-tech tanks with hardy plants where a simple timer and dimmer is all you need.
highlights: Six sizes, each covering a range of tank lengths
Inline controller with 3 timer settings, 7 brightness levels and sunrise/sunset (version 2)
watchOut: Not bright enough for demanding stem plants or carpets; version 1 units shipped without the controller.

name: B Series Ver.3
summary: Twinstar's budget WRGB line, now in its third version with Bluetooth control included. It gives clean whites and decent colour for low to medium light planted tanks, and it is a sensible pick for a first scape or a second tank.
bestFor: Low-tech tanks with Anubias, ferns, mosses, Cryptocorynes and easy stems, or anyone after an affordable app-controlled light.
highlights: Seven sizes from 20 cm to 130 cm
WRGB LEDs for natural colour on plants and fish
LightControl Standard Bluetooth controller included (timer, dimming, sunrise/sunset, Light Planner)
Low power draw, 10 W on the smallest to 52 W on the 120B

specs.Control: Bluetooth app (LightControl Standard included, no colour channel control)

watchOut: Twinstar itself says one 75B, 90B or 120B may be too weak for a planted tank of that length, and suggests running two.

name: C Series
summary: A lightweight RGB-W bar with telescopic legs that stretch up to about 15 cm, so one fixture can cover several tank lengths. Brightness is set with buttons on the light itself across 15 steps. The line has been discontinued, so you will mostly find it second hand or as remaining stock.
bestFor: Low to medium light tanks where you want flexible fitting across tank sizes and don't need an app.
highlights: Fits rimless glass up to 12 mm
watchOut: Discontinued, and there is no built-in timer mentioned, so plan on a plug timer.

name: E Series Ver.5
summary: Twinstar's mid-power line, sitting under the S Series in output but using the same fifth-generation LED mix of six colour channels plus dedicated plant-growth diodes. It suits planted tanks with a mix of easy and moderately demanding plants, and it comes in seven sizes from a 20 cm nano up to a 120 cm show tank.
bestFor: Medium-light planted tanks where you want good colour and app scheduling without paying for the S Series' extra punch.
highlights: Seven sizes covering 20 cm to 130 cm tanks
RGB plus plant-growth LEDs for strong colour rendering, especially on red plants
Bluetooth app control with timer, 100-step dimming, sunrise/sunset and a 25-day ramp-up planner
Draws roughly 20% less power than the matching S Series model
Slim metal body on legs that rest on rimless glass

specs.Control: Bluetooth app (LightControl Pro with 4-channel colour, or LightControl Standard)

watchOut: Buy the LightControl Pro version if you want to adjust the colour channels; the Standard controller only does brightness and timing.

name: EA Series (E IV)
summary: The fourth-generation E line, also sold as E IV. It added orange LEDs to the RGB mix, which makes green plants look particularly rich, and has adjustable legs plus a built-in dimmer. It is an older model now, replaced by E Series Ver.5.
bestFor: Medium-light rimless tanks where you like the look of a very thin fixture and want a simple dimmer.
highlights: Six sizes from 20 cm to 120 cm
RGB plus orange LEDs at 8300 K
watchOut: No app or timer; superseded by the Ver.5 E Series with Bluetooth control.

name: S Series Ver.5
summary: The strongest Twinstar line, built for high-tech tanks with CO2 and light-hungry plants like carpets and red stems. Version 5 pairs six colour channels with plant-growth LEDs and phone control, and the 600S and larger can be hung from a wire kit instead of sitting on legs.
bestFor: High-tech planted tanks running pressurised CO2 where you want plenty of headroom and fine control over colour.
highlights: Six sizes for 20 cm to 130 cm tanks
Highest output in the Twinstar range, up to 7,600 lm on the 1200S
Bluetooth app with timer, 100-step dimming, boost mode and sunrise/sunset
600S and up can be suspended with the optional wire kit

specs.Spectrum: RGB + plant-growth LEDs (6 colour channels), 400 to 780 nm
specs.Control: Bluetooth app (LightControl Pro with 4-channel colour, or LightControl Standard)
specs.Dimming: 100 steps, sunrise/sunset up to 60 min, boost mode
specs.Mounting: Rim legs; wire hanging kit for 600S and larger

watchOut: There is enough output here to cause algae in a tank without CO2 and good fertilising, so start well below full power.

name: SA Series (S IV)
summary: The fourth-generation S Series, a high-output bar that can sit on the rim or hang as a pendant with Twinstar's wire kit. It has a manual dimmer rather than an app, and packs enough light for demanding plants.
bestFor: High-light planted tanks where you want strong output and are happy to schedule it with a plug timer.
highlights: Six sizes from 20 cm to 120 cm
Up to 6,750 lm on the 1200 model
Rim mount or pendant with the optional wire kit
watchOut: No app or built-in timer, and the wire kit for hanging is sold separately.

name: SM Series
summary: The original Twinstar S light (later labelled SM), a bright fixture on fixed metal legs. It predates app control, and no dimmer or timer is listed for it.
bestFor: Rimless tanks matched to the exact light length where you run CO2 and use a plug timer.
highlights: Four sizes from 30 cm to 90 cm
Fixed metal legs for rimless tanks
Strong output for its era, up to 5,250 lm
watchOut: Legs don't adjust and there is no dimming mentioned, so it must match your tank length.

name: SP Series
summary: The suspended version of the older S Series, hung from above so the top of the tank stays open for maintenance. It has been discontinued but still turns up on larger display tanks.
bestFor: Larger high-tech tanks where you want a pendant look and room to reach in.
highlights: Three sizes for 60, 90 and 120 cm tanks
Hangs above the tank for an open top
watchOut: Discontinued, and you need a ceiling or bracket to hang it from.

name: Titan 1 RGB LED
summary: A 90 W hanging LED with 200 RGB diodes in a wide aluminium body. One unit covers a 60 to 90 cm tank, and the wide spread keeps the light even across the footprint rather than hot in the middle.
bestFor: Mid-size high-tech planted tanks where you want a pendant hung above an open-top rimless tank.
highlights: One unit covers a 60 to 90 cm tank; use two or more for bigger tanks
About 300 PAR directly under the light at 30 cm
Exposed heat-sink fins to shed heat

specs.Mounting: Suspension wires (97 cm) included; hanging kit sold separately

extra.Recommended hanging height: 30 cm or more above the tank

watchOut: It is designed to hang at least 30 cm above the water; the ceiling or hanging kit is sold separately.
